chunk_findings.detail: The spec in the intent states that phases are "counted done when all their items are done," but the aggregate line counts a phase as done only when the phase item's own `state == DONE`. Concretely: take a state with two phases, `P-a` and `P-b`, where every child of both has `state == DONE`, `P-a.state == DONE`, and `P-b` was never explicitly closed so `P-b.state != DONE`. `_phase_counts(items, "P-b")` returns `(n, n)`, so the very same function makes `P-b` appear in `closable`, i.e. the code itself asserts "all its items are done"; yet `sum(p.state == DONE for p in phases)` on line 43 yields `1`, so the report prints `phases 1/2 (50%), 1 ready to close` where the specified semantic requires `phases 2/2 (100%)`. The operator therefore sees a phase simultaneously reported as incomplete in the percentage and as finished ("ready to close"), and the headline phase percentage understates real progress. The fix is to count a phase done when `p.state == DONE` *or* `_phase_counts(items, p.id)` shows all children done (guarding the zero-child case), which is the same predicate already used for `closable`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/progress_line.py:43 (the `phases` numerator in `report`, mode "on")

chunk_findings.detail: The intent states the toggle is `[report].after_complete = on (default) | off | phase`, changed via `ddflow config --set`, but the test drives `run_cli(repo, "config", "session.progress_after_complete", "off")` — a different section and key (`session.progress_after_complete`) and a positional form rather than `--set`. Given input "config session.progress_after_complete off", if the implementation reads `report.after_complete` (as documented), the completion below still emits the `Progress:` block and the assertion `assert "Progress:" not in out` fails; conversely, if the implementation reads `session.progress_after_complete`, the documented `[report].after_complete` knob does nothing for operators. Either way the test does not verify the documented configuration path: it either fails or it silently validates an undocumented key. The direct-call check `PL.report(st, cfg, "T1", mode="off") == ""` covers only the in-process argument, not the config wiring the intent claims is tested.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_progress_line.py (test_off_suppresses_it_and_phase_shows_only_the_phase_and_next)

chunk_findings.detail: The config-driven "off" check is `assert "Progress:" not in out`, but `phase` mode output starts with `Phase P1:` and also contains no `Progress:` substring, so this assertion cannot distinguish `off` from `phase`. Concretely, if the config value `off` is mis-mapped to the `phase` mode, `complete T1` prints `Phase P1: 1/3 (33%)` (plus `Next: ...`) and the test still passes; only the earlier direct `PL.report(..., mode="off") == ""` call pins the real off semantics, leaving the intent's "off suppresses it" requirement unverified through the configuration path it advertises.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_progress_line.py (test_off_suppresses_it_and_phase_shows_only_the_phase_and_next)

chunk_findings.detail: The stated rule is "phases counted done when all their items are done", but the code counts a phase as done only when `p.state == DONE` (the phase's own state), while `_phase_counts` (used for the "current phase" line) measures completion by children. Concretely: a state containing a single phase `P` whose two child items are both `DONE` but whose own `state` is still `OPEN` (the operator has not run `ddflow complete P` yet) yields `phases 0/1 (0%)`, even though per the spec it should read `1/1 (100%)`; the same phase is simultaneously reported separately as `1 ready to close`, so the block both denies it is done and says it is closable. The `closable` computation right above (`p.state != DONE and … c[0] == c[1]`) shows the author is aware such phases exist, which makes the numerator's reliance on `p.state` the wrong predicate. The phase-mode line `Phase {phase}: {_pct(done, total)}` already uses the item-based definition, so the two lines in the same block disagree about what "done" means.

chunk_findings.detail: The test toggles suppression with `run_cli(repo, "config", "session.progress_after_complete", "off")`, then asserts `"Progress:" not in out`. That key and invocation do not match the interface this change specifies: the intent says the knob is `[report].after_complete = on (default) | off | phase`, “toggled by `ddflow config --set`”. If the implementation reads `report.after_complete` (as specified) while the config command silently accepts/creates the unrelated `session.progress_after_complete`, the write at line 70 is a no-op, the report stays on, and the final `assert "Progress:" not in out` fails — the test is exercising a key that has no effect on the feature. Either the test targets the wrong config path or the implementation exposes a key other than the documented one; both cannot be true.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_progress_line.py:70 (`test_off_suppresses_it_and_phase_shows_only_the_phase_and_next`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The test name promises “only the phase and next”, but the assertions are `not short.startswith("Progress:")` and `short.startswith("Phase P1:")`. A regression in which `mode="phase"` returns the per-phase header *followed by* the whole global block (e.g. `"Phase P1: 1/3 (33%)\nProgress: tasks 1/3 …"`) satisfies both predicates, so the exclusivity the change is supposed to guarantee is never actually checked — anything after the first line is unconstrained. A concrete input that would slip through: phase mode returning `"Phase P1: …\nProgress: tasks 1/3 (33%) · bugs … · phases …"` passes the test even though the global report leaked into phase mode.

Note: the output shape the tests assert (a dedicated `Phase P1: 1/3 (33%)` line via exact `lines` membership, and a separate `Next: ` line) also diverges from the single `·`-joined example given in the intent (`… · current P-agent-hygiene 2/11 (18%) · next: B-hy-stop-protocol …`), but since the intent also says “a few lines” I did not count that as a defect.

data.body: complete (CLI, and MCP via B-hy-progress-mcp) appends a compact block, well under 100 tokens, e.g. 'Progress: tasks 377/614 (61%) · bugs fixed 287/298 (96%), 11 open (2 high) · phases 23/62 (37%), 6 ready to close' / 'Phase P-agent-hygiene: 1/12 (8%)' / 'Next: ...' (or 'Next (when a slot frees): ...' when only the parallelism cap holds ready work). A phase counts as done by its own state (completed through its phase pipeline); a phase whose items are all done but which was never closed is counted separately as 'ready to close', so the total never claims a closure that did not happen. Counts come from the folded state plus one schedule.plan call. Knob [session].progress_after_complete = on (default) | phase (the phase line and next only) | off, set with 'ddflow config session.progress_after_complete off' or by asking the agent; the MCP instructions tell the agent to relay the block verbatim. Test: content, size budget, modes, cap-held next.
